text: What does wind down mean? LIV Golf to wind down in Nov. 2026. To wind down means to bring a business or organization to an orderly end by gradually closing its operations. LIV Golf announced on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, that it will wind down, after a rescue financing deal with backer BC Partners fell through.. LIV Golf said on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, that it will liquidate after its last-ditch financing deal with BC Partners collapsed. Several leading players had already left the league.. LIV Golf, the breakaway men's golf tour formed in 2021, said the league would close in an orderly way rather than continue. Its board special committee, led by Gene Davis and Jon Zinman, called this the most responsible course for the league at this time. The league said it would stay open to offers from third parties that could add value during the process. The league had lined up $300 million in possible financing from BC Partners to stage tournaments in 2027. Several notable players chose not to commit to the league, and the plan was dropped. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the main backer, had invested more than $5 billion since 2022 and had said in April that LIV no longer matched its investment strategy. The 2026 season has now been completed. The shutdown ends a rivalry that began in June 2022, when LIV's first event was held at the Centurion Club near St Albans, Hertfordshire, England. Its players, including Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau, had competed against the PGA Tour, which suspended members who joined LIV. LIV never secured a long-term U.S. Television partner, which limited its audience and revenue there.

Oleshky ceasefire: Melania Trump brokered a Ukraine-Russia truce in Nov. 2026. The Oleshky ceasefire is a temporary, limited humanitarian truce between Ukrainian and Russian forces in Oleshky, a village in Ukraine that Russia occupied during its full-scale invasion in 2022. First lady Melania Trump helped broker it, and officials from both countries praised it at the White House in early November 2026.. Kirill Dimitrov, an envoy of Vladimir Putin, thanked Melania Trump at the White House on a Thursday in early November 2026 for brokering the Oleshky truce. A video of the exchange was published by The Guardian.. Kirill Dimitrov, an envoy of Russian President Vladimir Putin, gave Melania Trump a gift at the White House on a Thursday to thank her for her role in the truce. On the day of the event, Melania Trump and peace envoys from Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House. Melania Trump described the truce as a possible "spark" for a longer-lasting peace, and said on Nov. 5, 2026 that both countries had chosen "humanity over war" by following through on the agreement. The truce matters now because it is one of the few concrete results so far from a diplomatic effort led by the first lady, and it followed a visit by Russian and Ukrainian delegations to the White House. Fox News also reported that the White House hosted the talks, and a Fox News report described the arrangement as a temporary, limited pause.

What does designated for assignment mean? DFA in baseball. Designated for assignment, or DFA, means an MLB team has removed a player from its 40-man roster. The club then has up to seven days to trade him, put him on waivers, or release him. Waivers take 48 hours, so in practice a team has about five days to find a trade.. MLB teams clear 40-man roster spots ahead of the Nov. 17, 2026 Rule 5 protection deadline, and DFA moves pile up each November.. If another team claims the player on waivers, it takes over his contract. If no one claims him, his team can send him outright to the minors, though veterans with enough service time can refuse and become free agents. The player keeps being paid while he waits; that waiting period is often called "DFA limbo." The days between Christmas and New Year's Day do not count toward the seven. DFAs come in waves in November. Teams must add prospects to the 40-man roster by Nov. 17, 2026 to protect them from the Rule 5 draft, and the non-tender deadline follows on Nov. 20, so clubs clear spots by designating fringe players. A player picked up in the Rule 5 draft cannot be designated from the draft until 20 days before Opening Day, and a player just claimed off waivers cannot be designated again for at least 48 hours.

How is the MLB MVP voted? 30 writers, results Nov. 12. The MLB MVP is chosen by 30 members of the Baseball Writers' Association of America, two from each big league city, voting separately for the American and National League. Each lists 10 players; first place earns 14 points, then 9 down to 1. The 2026 MVPs will be announced Nov. 12.. MLB's 2026 award winners are announced Nov. 9-12, ending with the American and National League MVPs on Nov. 12.. The same writers' group picks the other main awards, with 30 voters each. The Cy Young ballot has five places worth 7, 4, 3, 2 and 1 points. Rookie of the Year and Manager of the Year ballots have three places worth 5, 3 and 1. Writers cannot split a place between two players, and AL cities vote only on AL awards, NL cities only on NL awards. Ballots are turned in before the postseason begins, so October heroics do not count. The 2026 schedule runs across one week on MLB Network: Rookie of the Year on Monday, Nov. 9, Manager of the Year on Nov. 10, Cy Young on Nov. 11 and MVP on Thursday, Nov. 12. Three finalists are named in advance for each award, and full vote totals are published after each announcement.

What does non-tender mean in baseball? MLB deadline is Nov. 20. To non-tender a player means an MLB team declines to offer him a contract for next season, so he becomes a free agent at once. It mostly happens to arbitration-eligible players whose next salary would be higher than the team wants to pay. The 2026 non-tender deadline is 4 p.m. Central on Nov. 20.. MLB's 2026 non-tender deadline falls on Nov. 20, less than two weeks before the labor agreement expires on Dec. 1.. Players with fewer than six years in the majors are still under team control. Each winter the team must "tender" them a contract by the deadline to keep them. Those eligible for salary arbitration can get large raises on their second, third and fourth trips through the process, so a club may let a useful but costly player go rather than risk an arbitrator's number. Teams also non-tender players with injury questions, or to free a spot on the 40-man roster. Non-tendered players skip waivers, can sign with any team, and sometimes return to their old club on a cheaper deal. This year the deadline carries extra weight. The labor agreement between owners and players expires at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Dec. 1, 2026, and owners are widely expected to lock players out the next day. During a lockout, major league transactions freeze, so players cut on Nov. 20 would have only about 11 days to sign before the market could stop.

What is a qualifying offer in MLB? $23.15 million, decide by Nov. 17. A qualifying offer is a one-year contract that an MLB team can offer its own departing free agent. For the 2026-27 offseason it is worth $23.15 million, the average of the 125 highest salaries in baseball. Players have until 3 p.m. Central on Nov. 17 to accept; if one declines and signs elsewhere, his old team gets a draft pick.. MLB teams made qualifying offers to eight free agents after the 2026 World Series, and the players must decide by Nov. 17.. Eight players received the offer in early November 2026: Randy Arozarena (Mariners), Jake Bauers (Brewers), David Bednar (Yankees), Ryan Jeffers (Twins), Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrián Morejón (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles) and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs). The amount is a record, up from $22.025 million a year earlier. A team can make the offer only if the player spent the whole season with it, and a player can receive one only once in his career. A player who accepts cannot be traded without his consent until June 15. The draft pick is what makes the offer matter. The pick the old team receives depends on its finances and the size of the new contract: a revenue-sharing team losing a player who signs for $50 million or more gets a pick after the first round, while a team that paid the luxury tax gets one only after the fourth round. The team that signs him pays a price too: a club over the luxury tax forfeits its second- and fifth-highest picks plus $1 million in international bonus money. Last offseason 13 players got the offer and 4 accepted it: Trent Grisham, Shota Imanaga, Gleyber Torres and Brandon Woodruff. This year the rule may be living its final winter: the labor contract that created it expires at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Dec. 1, 2026, and a new deal could change or drop it.

What is the Rule 5 draft? MLB protection deadline is Nov. 17. The Rule 5 draft lets MLB teams take minor league players that other clubs have left off their 40-man rosters. A pick costs $100,000, and the new team must keep the player on its major league active roster all season or offer him back for $50,000. Clubs must decide whom to protect by 6 p.m. Eastern on Nov. 17, 2026.. MLB teams must set their 40-man rosters for Rule 5 protection by Nov. 17, 2026, ahead of a draft that a possible lockout could delay.. Eligibility depends on age and time in the system. A player who signed at 18 or younger becomes eligible before his fifth Rule 5 draft; one who signed at 19 or older, before his fourth. The rule exists so teams cannot hoard young players in the minors while other clubs would use them in the majors. Its name simply comes from its place, rule 5, in baseball's rulebook; the draft has been held every year since 1920. Some bargains became stars. The Pirates took Roberto Clemente from the Brooklyn Dodgers with the first pick in 1954, and Johan Santana, drafted in 1999, went on to win two Cy Young Awards with Minnesota. Josh Hamilton, Shane Victorino and Dan Uggla were also Rule 5 picks. The 2026 draft is scheduled for Dec. 9 at the Winter Meetings in San Diego, but it is in doubt. The labor deal expires Dec. 1, and in the 2021 lockout the major league phase was postponed while the minor league phase, which costs $24,000 per pick for Triple-A players, went ahead. The players' union has proposed moving this year's draft into November.
